hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to the close-up visual structure of an eye, characterized by the concentric geometry of a dark central pupil or ring surrounded by a colored iris, almost always featuring a sharp, bright white specular highlight or catchlight that indicates a glossy surface. The activating features are dominated by a central black or dark brown circle set against an iris of amber, gold, honey-brown, or pale blue, framed by textured organic surroundings of russet-orange, beige, or brown fur, or wet, mottled green skin. The background typically consists of defocused, neutral tones such as olive green, soft beige, or deep black, creating a depth-of-field effect that isolates the sharp details of the eye. The neuron remains invariant to the specific biological species (activating for canines, foxes, amphibians, humans, and even stylized or structural eye-mimics) and the texture of the surrounding material, provided the high-contrast, glossy, concentric eye pattern is preserved. The eye feature typically occupies 5–20% of the image area and is positioned centrally or slightly off-center to the left or right.
